title: Natalie Wood
wiki_lead:
Natalie Wood (née Zacharenko; July 20, 1938 – November 29, 1981) was an American actress. She began acting at age four and co-starred at age eight in Miracle on 34th Street (1947). As a teenager, she was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her performance in Rebel Without a Cause (1955), followed by a role in John Ford's The Searchers (1956).
Wood starred in the musical films West Side Story (1961) and Gypsy (1962) and received nominations for an Academy Award for Best Actress for her performances in Splendor in the Grass (1961) and Love with the Proper Stranger (1963). Her career continued with films such as Sex and the Single Girl (1964), The Great Race (1965), Inside Daisy Clover (1965), This Property Is Condemned, Penelope (1966), and Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice (1969).
During the 1970s, Wood began a hiatus from film and had two daughters: one with Robert Wagner, her first husband, and one with her second husband, Richard Gregson. She acted in only two feature films throughout the decade, but she appeared slightly more often in television productions, including a remake of From Here to Eternity (1979) for which she won a Golden Globe Award. Wood's films represented a "coming of age" for her and for Hollywood films in general. Critics have suggested that her cinematic career represents a portrait of modern American womanhood in transition because she was one of the few to take both child roles and those of middle-aged characters.
On November 29, 1981, at the age of 43, Wood drowned in the Pacific Ocean at Santa Catalina Island during a break from production of her would-be comeback film Brainstorm (1983). She was with her husband Wagner and Brainstorm co-star Christopher Walken. The events surrounding her death have been the subject of conflicting witness statements, prompting the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, under the instruction of the coroner's office, to list her cause of death as "drowning and other undetermined factors" in 2012. In 2018, Wagner was named as a person of interest in the ongoing investigation into her death.

Early life
Wood was born Natalie Zacharenko in San Francisco on July 20, 1938, to Maria Zoudilova (sometimes transliterated Zoodiloff) and second husband Nicholas Zacharenko. She was of Russian descent, and raised in the Russian Orthodox Church. Her mother, who also used the names Mary, Marie, and Musia, was from Barnaul, Russia. 
Wood's maternal grandfather owned soap and candle factories, and an estate outside Barnaul. With the start of the Russian Civil War, his family fled Russia for China, settling as refugees in Harbin. Her mother was previously married to the Armenian mechanic Alexander Tatuloff from 1925 to 1936. They had a daughter named Olga (1928–2015) and moved to America by ship in 1930, before divorcing six years later.

grok_lead: Natalie Wood (born Natalia Nikolaevna Zakharenko; July 20, 1938 â November 29, 1981) was an American actress renowned for her transition from child stardom to acclaimed adult roles in Hollywood cinema. Born in San Francisco to Russian immigrant parents Nikolai and Maria Gurdin, she began performing at age four and gained early fame as a child actor. Over her four-decade career, Wood starred in over 70 films and television productions, earning three Academy Award nominationsâincluding for Rebel Without a Cause (1955), Splendor in the Grass (1961), and Love with the Proper Stranger (1963)âand a Golden Globe for her versatile portrayals in dramas, musicals, and comedies. Her death by drowning off Catalina Island at age 43, initially ruled accidental but later reclassified as undetermined, has fueled ongoing investigations and public interest as of 2024. Wood's early career was propelled by her mother's ambitious management, leading to her film debut in Happy Land (1943) at age four. She achieved breakout success with the role of Susan Walker in the holiday classic Miracle on 34th Street (1947), which showcased her natural charm and established her as a prominent child star. As a teenager, Wood navigated the challenges of maturing in the industry, earning her first Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actress as Judy in Nicholas Ray's Rebel Without a Cause (1955), opposite James Dean and Sal Mineo, a film that defined 1950s youth rebellion. Her transition to adult roles in the early 1960s brought further acclaim, including a second Academy Award nomination for Best Actress in Elia Kazan's Splendor in the Grass (1961) as Deanie Loomis, alongside Warren Beatty, a third for Love with the Proper Stranger (1963), and iconic performances as Maria in Robert Wise's West Side Story (1961) and the titular Gypsy Rose Lee in Gypsy (1962). In her later career, Wood balanced acting with family life, appearing in notable films like The Searchers (1956) with John Wayne, Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice (1969), and her final role in Brainstorm (1983, released posthumously). Personally, she married actor Robert Wagner twiceâfirst from 1957 to 1962 and again from 1972 until her deathâand British producer Richard Gregson from 1969 to 1972; she had two daughters, Natasha Gregson Wagner (born 1970) and Courtney Wagner (born 1974). Wood's lifelong hydrophobia, stemming from a childhood accident, added poignancy to the circumstances of her death during a boating trip with Wagner and actor Christopher Walken. Despite career hiatuses for motherhood, her legacy endures as a symbol of Hollywood's golden age, with her films continuing to influence popular culture.
